payload.prompt: Total costs increased significantly from January to February 2026. Analyze the general ledger and identify the three expense accounts with the largest increase in amount. Create an internal project for each of the three accounts using the account name. Also create an activity for each project.

payload.goal: Analyze the general ledger for January vs February 2026, identify the three expense accounts with the largest cost increase, then create one internal project per account (named after the account) and one activity per project.
success_checks: General ledger queried for period 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-31 and 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28
Three expense accounts with largest month-over-month increase identified and documented
Three internal projects created, each named after one of the identified expense accounts
One activity created and linked to each of the three projects
All projects marked as internal (not customer-facing)
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty — no ledger data exists; real ledger data must be present in the target environment for analysis to be meaningful
Expense account range not specified (e.g., 4000–8999 in Norwegian chart of accounts); assumption is standard Norwegian expense accounts
If multiple accounts have equal increases, tie-breaking rule is undefined — risk of arbitrary selection
Activity type/name not specified in prompt; a generic activity name will be used per project
Project start/end dates not provided; projects may require dates depending on system configuration
Internal project flag must be set correctly to avoid billing implications
VAT not applicable to this task
payload.suggested_first_action: GET /ledger?dateFrom=2026-01-01&dateTo=2026-01-31&accountType=EXPENSE to retrieve January expense ledger entries, then repeat for February, and compute delta per account.
ordered_steps: 1. GET /ledger/account?isActive=true to retrieve full chart of accounts and filter for expense accounts (typically account numbers 4000–8999 in Norwegian standard)
2. GET /ledger?dateFrom=2026-01-01&dateTo=2026-01-31 filtered by expense account range to aggregate total debit/credit amounts per account for January 2026
3. GET /ledger?dateFrom=2026-02-01&dateTo=2026-02-28 filtered by expense account range to aggregate total debit/credit amounts per account for February 2026
4. Compute delta (February amount minus January amount) per expense account and sort descending to identify top 3 accounts with largest increase
5. Record account number and account name for each of the three identified accounts
6. POST /project with body {name: '<AccountName_1>', isInternal: true, projectType: 'INTERNAL'} to create project for account #1
7. POST /project with body {name: '<AccountName_2>', isInternal: true, projectType: 'INTERNAL'} to create project for account #2
8. POST /project with body {name: '<AccountName_3>', isInternal: true, projectType: 'INTERNAL'} to create project for account #3
9. POST /project/activity with body {project: {id: <project1_id>}, name: 'Activity - <AccountName_1>'} to create activity for project 1
10. POST /project/activity with body {project: {id: <project2_id>}, name: 'Activity - <AccountName_2>'} to create activity for project 2
11. POST /project/activity with body {project: {id: <project3_id>}, name: 'Activity - <AccountName_3>'} to create activity for project 3
12. Verify all three projects and activities are visible via GET /project and GET /project/activity

planned_endpoints.summary: Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.
Find projects corresponding with sent data.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedPrice=<amount> (camelCase).
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.

payload.headline: Wrong top-3 expense accounts identified; 3/5 scoring checks failed despite correct project/activity creation
what_went_wrong: The agent's ledger analysis produced incorrect top-3 accounts — scoring checks 1, 2, and 4 failed, indicating the identified accounts or their ranking was wrong.
Two 400 errors from bad nested field syntax ('id;number;name' not valid for AccountDTO) wasted calls and may have caused incomplete data retrieval.
The agent relied on trimmed/summarized API responses without verifying completeness — it may have missed accounts or misread amounts from paginated results.
No pagination handling: the agent fetched ledger postings without checking 'count' vs 'from'/'count' parameters, likely missing entries and skewing totals.
what_worked: Project and activity creation was correct — checks 3 and 5 passed, all 3 projects and linked activities were successfully created.
Internal project flag (isInternal=true) and project activity linking via /project/projectActivity worked correctly.
what_to_try_next: Fix field filter syntax for nested account fields (use 'account(id,number,name)' format) and verify pagination by checking total 'count' and fetching all pages before aggregating.
Use /ledger/account endpoint to get the full chart of accounts first, then filter postings per account to ensure no accounts are missed in the comparison.
After computing increases, log all account totals explicitly before selecting top-3 to catch data gaps — the correct top-3 likely included different accounts than 7100, 6500, 5000.
unnecessary_calls: Two failed GET /ledger/posting calls with bad field filter 'id;number;name' for AccountDTO — should have used correct nested syntax from the start.
search_tripletex_api for 'activity project activity' was redundant given the agent already knew the /activity and /project/projectActivity endpoints.
